newsitem.title: UK: Analysts blase, admiring of Zeneca results.
newsitem.headline: Analysts blase, admiring of Zeneca results.

text.p: Zeneca Group Plc's billion pound pre-tax profits for 1996 met with an almost blase response from analysts on Tuesday.

The 1.011 billion stg pretax profit before exceptionals was only a shade above the narrow forecast range of between 992 million and 1.010 billion predicted by analysts, who said the results had been well flagged in the group's January trading statement.
However, despite the lack of surprises, there was widespread admiration of the group's performance and prospects.

Panmure Gordon analyst Robin Gilbert said the results "were boringly in line," but added that Zeneca's management "have done outstandingly well since the divorce from ICI (in 1993) and can look forward to the future with confidence."
Yamaichi International analyst Erling Refsum said "it is a very strong story. A very solid reassuring, comforting result."

Analysts were also inclined to support Zeneca chief executive David Barnes's view that the group's share price, which briefly surged to a new record of 19.38 stg in morning trading, was fully justified on fundamentals and did not include any potential bid premium.

Yamaichi's Refsum said "I think a lot of people will focus on the fact that there is no need for a bid premium to justify their current share price, so you could add in a premium for the takeover potential."

Panmure Gordon's Gilbert added: "In a sense there should be a bid premium in view of the fact that it is an attractive mid-sized company in an industry that is consolidating," although he said he did not expect an imminent bid.
Suggestions that the company faced a product gap when its best-selling product, heart drug Zestril, loses patent in 2001 were also brushed a side.

Some traders attributed the 2.2 percent fall in Zeneca's share price in late trading to concerns the company could face a hiatus in products after Zestril's expiry. But Panmure's Gilbert said "They have got one of the richest pipelines around to replace it."
James Culverwell, analyst at Merrill Lynch, said the results "were exactly in line, with some good new products doing well."
Culverwell said he expected "significant growth" in the next few years and retained his accumulate stance on Zeneca's stock.

Merrill Lynch is not altering its 1997 forecasts as a result of Tuesday's announcements and Panmure's Gilbert said he was also maintaining his 1997 pre-tax profit forecast of 1.120 billion stg and earnings per share of 78.0 pence.
